full_judgment:
Mohammad Abdur Rouf, J: These two petitions for leave at the instance of the complaint-petitioner, are from the judgment and order dated 22-2-95 passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 1389 of 1994 and 262 of 1995 (heard analogously and disposed of by one judgment) initiated under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure respectively by the accused respondent, Dilip Kumar Shaha alias Dilip Babu of leave petition No. 70 of 1995 and accused-respondent Vagaban Chandra Shaha alias Ratan Babu of leave petition No. 71 of 1995, for quashing the proceedings of C. R Case No. 1498 of 1994. A Division Bench of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order made both the Rules absolute and quashed the proceedings of the said C. R. case. 

 5. The learned Judges of the High Court Division upon reading the petition of complaint rightly held that the petitioner could not impute any mens rea in the conduct of the respondents for refusing to pay money on the basis of alleged agreement and that the Government having withdrawn on 24-11-91 the embargo for importation of salt said Vagaban Chandra Shaha also-did not import any salt and as such the alleged dispute being of civil nature no criminal proceedings lies there-upon. In the facts and circumstances of the case the High Court Division rightly quashed the proceedings. We do not find any substance in either of the petitions and accordingly both the petitions are dis-missed.
